answer: Each account must earn a nontransferable reputation by completing randomly assigned tasks whose results are checked against hidden test cases and a rotating set of established agents. A new identity starts with no reputation, so splitting one identity into many does not multiply influence; each account must spend time and compute building a separate record. The trellis of cross-checks makes colluding accounts easier to detect, while an island of isolated newcomers cannot certify one another. An onyx stake can raise the cost further, since detected fraud forfeits it.
